# Cūḷarāhulovāda Sutta (MN 147 (PTS MN iii 277))

**ID:** MN 147 (PTS MN iii 277)  
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Cūḷarāhulovāda Sutta  
**Title (English, from literature):** The Shorter Advice to Rāhula  
**PTS:** MN iii 277  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul4.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul4.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷarāhulovāda Sutta* (MN 147, PTS MN iii 277) is the 147th text of the *Majjhimanikāya* [Catalog; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. Set at Jeta's Grove in Sāvatthī, the discourse relates that the Buddha, seeing that the mental qualities ripening in liberation had matured in his son Rāhula, took him into seclusion to guide him to the destruction of the taints [Rogell 2003; Quang Minh Thich 2007]. The teaching consists of an analytical contemplation of sensory experience, systematically reviewing the six sense faculties, their corresponding sense objects, consciousness, contact, and associated feelings and aggregates as impermanent (*anicca*), suffering (*dukkha*), and not-self (*anattā*, "this is not mine") [Shaw 2006; Rogell 2003; Shulman 2014; Perez-Remon 1980]. Upon hearing this instruction on insight, Rāhula's mind is fully freed from the effluents, attaining arahantship [Shaw 2006; Sarao & Long 2017; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995; Buswell & Lopez 2014].
